children.translated_text: being, in his last existence, seeking [the right conditions for his final] conduct, having grasped the path to liberation, turned inward toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, turned outward from <s>saṃsāra</s>, desiring nothing, bearing his last body among all the courses of existence with their deaths and rebirths—having passed away from a certain class of gods, he descended into the womb of that woman of noble birth. There are five special qualities found in certain wise women of the maternal kind. What five? She knows when a man is passionate. She knows when he is free from passion. She knows the [right] time. She knows the fertile period. She knows when an embryo has descended. She knows from whom the embryo has descended. She knows if it is a boy. She knows if it is a girl. If it is a boy, it rests supported by the right side of the womb. If it is a girl, it rests supported by the left side of the womb. She, delighted and joyful, informed her husband: "Fortunate, O noble son, may you prosper! I have become pregnant. And since [the child] rests supported by the right side of my womb, it will certainly be a boy." He too, delighted and joyful, uttered an exclamation: "May I indeed see the face of a son long desired! May he be well-born for me, not ill-born! May he perform my duties, when maintained may he maintain me in return, may he receive the inheritance, and may my family lineage be long-lasting! And knowing her to be pregnant, he kept her on the upper floor of the palace, unrestricted, with cold provisions in the cold season and warm provisions in the warm season, with foods prescribed by physicians—not too bitter, not too sour, not too salty, not too sweet, not too pungent, not too astringent, devoid of bitter, sour, salty, sweet, pungent, and astringent [extremes]—her body adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, like an <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymph) wandering in the <s>Nandana</s> grove, not descending from couch to couch, from seat to seat, to the ground below. Nor was there any hearing of unpleasant sounds for her, until the maturation of the embryo. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born—handsome, pleasing to look at, inspiring confidence, fair, of golden complexion, with an umbrella-shaped head, with arms reaching to his knees, with a broad and wide forehead, with joined eyebrows, with a prominent nose, adorned with an ear-ornament set with jewels. The householder <s>Balasena</s>, having summoned jewel-appraisers, said: "Sirs, determine the value of these jewels." "It is not possible to determine the value of these jewels," [they replied]. It is indeed the custom that when the value of a jewel cannot be determined, its value is set at a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million). They said: "O householder, the value of these jewels is a <s>koṭi</s>." children.translated_text: He named one <s>Dāsaka</s> (Little Servant) and the other <s>Pālaka</s> (Protector). <s>Śroṇa Koṭīkarṇa</s> was entrusted to eight nurses: two shoulder-nurses, two play-nurses, two washing-nurses, and two milk-nurses. He was raised and nurtured by eight nurses with milk, yogurt, butter, clarified butter, the cream of clarified butter, and other choice prepared provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. When he had grown up, he was instructed in writing, arithmetic, calculation, accounting, deposits, withdrawals, trusts, the examination of buildings, and the examination of jewels. He became expert in these eight examinations—articulate, learned, clever in conduct. His father had three seasonal residences built for him: one for winter, one for summer, and one for the rainy season. Three gardens were laid out: for winter, summer, and the rainy season. Three inner apartments were provided: for the eldest, the middle, and the youngest [wives]. On the upper floor of the palace, he enjoyed himself, took pleasure, and amused himself with music played without [the presence of] men. The householder <s>Balasena</s> was always occupied with agricultural work. <s>Koṭīkarṇa</s> saw his father

children.translated_text: always occupied with agricultural work. He said: "Father, for whose sake are you always occupied with agricultural work?" He replied: "Son, just as you enjoy yourself, take pleasure, and amuse yourself on the upper floor of the palace with music played without men—if I too were to enjoy myself, take pleasure, and amuse myself in the same way, before long our wealth would become diminished, exhausted, and consumed." He reflected: "The reproach is directed at me." He said: "Father, if that is so, I shall take merchandise and go to another country." The father replied: "Son, I have so much wealth in jewels that even if you were to spend the jewels at the rate of sesame, rice, jujubes, and horse-gram, still my jewels would not be exhausted." He said: "Father, give me permission; I shall go to another country with merchandise." <s>Balasena</s>, knowing his firm determination, gave permission. The householder <s>Balasena</s> had a bell-announcement made in the village of <s>Vāsava</s>: "Whoever among you is willing to cross the great ocean together with the caravan-leader <s>Śroṇa Koṭīkarṇa</s>, without toll and without tax, let him prepare merchandise for the ocean voyage." children.translated_text: ) <s>Śroṇa Koṭīkarṇa</s> would travel by vehicle. He considered: 'If [travelling] by elephants—elephants are delicate and difficult to maintain. Horses too are delicate and difficult to maintain. Donkeys are intelligent and delicate. Let him go by donkey-vehicle.' He was summoned by his father and told: 'Son, you must not go at the front of the caravan, nor at the rear. If a strong robber attacks, he falls upon the front of the caravan; if weak, he falls upon the rear. You must travel in the middle of the caravan, lest when the caravan-leader is killed, the caravan be destroyed.' The servants <s>Dāsaka</s> and <s>Pālaka</s> were also instructed: 'Sons, you two must not, by any means, let <s>Śroṇa Koṭīkarṇa</s> out of your sight.' Then, at another time, <s>Śroṇa Koṭīkarṇa</s>, having performed the auspicious ceremonies, rites, and benedictions, approached his mother, fell at her feet, and said: 'Mother, I am going. Look upon me! I am setting out upon the great ocean.' She began to weep. He said: 'Mother, why do you weep?' The mother, with tearful and sorrowful face, said: 'Son, will I perhaps see my boy alive again?' He reflected: 'I have set out with auspicious [rites]. (

body.translated_text: Proceeding gradually through villages, towns, market-towns, hamlets, and trading cities, he reached the shore of the great ocean. Having carefully boarded a seagoing vessel, he descended into the great ocean as a wealth-seeker. With favorable wind, he reached the Jewel Island. There, having carefully examined [the gems], he filled that vessel with jewels, just as [one fills a container] with sesame, rice, jujubes, and horse-beans. With favorable wind, having successfully completed the sea-voyage, he reached <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. The caravan halted on that very seashore. That <s>Śroṇa Koṭīkarṇa</s>, the caravan-leader, taking <s>Dāsaka</s> and <s>Pālaka</s>, withdrew from the midst of the caravan to a secluded spot and began to calculate income and expenditure. Afterward, he instructed the servant <s>Dāsaka</s>: '<s>Dāsaka</s>, go see what the caravan is doing.' He went. He saw the caravan sleeping. He too fell asleep right there. Since <s>Dāsaka</s> was taking too long, he instructed <s>Pālaka</s>: '<s>Pālaka</s>, go see what the caravan is doing.' He went. He saw the caravan cooking porridge. They say: "The fruit and ripening of this <s>karma</s> is unpleasant. Desist from this sinful, unwholesome practice."' She said: 'Sir, my mother and father passed away twelve years ago. Is there anyone you have seen who, having gone to the other world, has come back again?' He said: 'I myself have come [back].' She did not believe him. He said: 'Sister, if you do not believe, in your ancestral family house there are four iron chests filled with gold. And in the middle is a golden staff and water-pot. They say: "Retrieve them, and with them treat yourself to proper happiness, and offer food in due course to the noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, and make a gift of merit (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) in our name. Perhaps this <s>karma</s> may become attenuated, exhausted, and completely consumed."' She reflected: 'I have never heard such a thing before. Let me see—if this all turns out to be true.' She went and had it dug up, and found everything exactly as described. Then she believed.

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to <s>Śroṇa Koṭīkarṇa</s>: "It is not the proper time, <s>Śroṇa</s>, for answering the questions. The questions should be asked in the midst of the <s>Saṅgha</s>. There will be the proper time for answering the questions." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having risen early in the morning, sat down on the seat prepared before the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks). Then the venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīkarṇa</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, paid homage with his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, he said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "In the <s>Aśmāparāntaka</s> regions, in <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>, Venerable Sir, dwells <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> who is my <s>upādhyāya</s> (preceptor). He pays homage with his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, asks about freedom from illness and comfortable abiding, and presents five questions in detail as previously stated, up to 'to whom are they forfeitable?'" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Therefore I authorize the following: In the frontier regions, <s>upasaṃpadā</s> (ordination) by a group of five with a <s>Vinaya</s> expert as the fifth. Bathing at all times. Single-layered sandals are to be worn, not double-folded or triple-folded. If those become worn out, having attached a clasp, they are to be worn. When a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) sends robes to another <s>bhikṣu</s>, and they are lost in transit—departed from here but not arrived there—they are forfeitable to no one."

body.translated_text: The venerable <s>Upāli</s> asks the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "The <s>Bhagavān</s> has said, 'In the frontier regions, <s>upasaṃpadā</s> (ordination) by a group of five with a <s>Vinaya</s> expert as the fifth.' What is the central region and what is the frontier?" "To the east, <s>Upāli</s>, there is a city called <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>; to its east is a forest called <s>Puṇḍrakakṣa</s>. That is the central region. Beyond that is the frontier. To the south is a city called <s>Śarāvatī</s>; beyond it is a river called <s>Śarāvatī</s>. That is the central region. Beyond that is the frontier. To the west are two Brahmin villages called <s>Sthūṇa</s> and <s>Upasthūṇaka</s>. That is the central region. Beyond that is the frontier. To the north is <s>Uśīragiri</s>. That is the central region. Beyond that is the frontier."

children.translated_text: Because he performed service to the <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, and made a vow, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, he was born in a wealthy family of great riches and great possessions. Having gone forth in my teaching, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), he has directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (the state of an arhat). I, by that <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, have been equaled in strength, equaled in speed, equaled in endurance, equaled in common attainments — the teacher has been pleased, not displeased. For indeed, monks, of exclusively dark <s>karmas</s>, the result is exclusively dark; of exclusively bright <s>karmas</s>, the result is exclusively bright; of mixed <s>karmas</s>, the result is mixed. Therefore, monks, having cast away exclusively dark <s>karmas</s> and mixed ones, effort should be directed toward exclusively bright <s>karmas</s> alone. Thus, monks, should you train yourselves. The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) said: 'Because he uttered harsh words toward his mother, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, he saw the lower realms of existence in this very life.'

children.translated_text: and upon seeing them, they asked: 'Where will you gentlemen arrange this bed fit for a god?' <s>Upananda</s> said: 'In my own dwelling.' 'Whose bed is being taken?' <s>Upananda</s> said: 'It was obtained by me.' They grumbled, criticized, and reproached: 'Is the venerable <s>Upananda</s>, the ascetic, troubled by sensual pleasures?' Having gone to the monastery, the monastery was sprinkled and swept, a fine cow-dung paste was applied, and having arranged the bed, he thought: 'I shall recline.' And the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) arrived at that place. Filled with pride, he said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Look, Venerable One, what kind of bed I have!' Thereupon the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'From the very beginning, monks, <s>Upananda</s>, the foolish man, should be known as one who conceals faults.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> reflected: 'Whatever disadvantage arises when monks arrange beds on high and great couches — therefore a monk should not sit on a high or great couch. If one does sit, there is a transgression.'

body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. He reflected: 'I am <s>Upananda</s> — I desire even a proper bed. I shall not bear the name <s>Upananda</s> if I do not procure a bed or a couch.' Early in the morning, he went to the presence of King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>. The king said to him: 'Welcome to the venerable <s>Upananda</s>! Has the venerable <s>Upananda</s> slept well?' He said: 'Blockhead, do you not know that I arrange a bed of eight layers? <s>Upananda</s> does the same. I am a newcomer to the <s>saṃgha</s>; in my turn, a creaking bedstead was allotted to me. I turn about in fear, thinking it might break. The venerable <s>Upananda</s> has such an eight-layered bed — well arranged, excellently arranged! Where was it rejected, and by whom? If it pleases you, let it be taken.' <s>Upananda</s> said: 'Does the kingdom of <s>Kosala</s> belong to me? Have it sent to the monastery.' The king assigned eight men to him. By him an order was given to the cowherd: 'Kill this calf, take its hide, bring it to the venerable <s>Upananda</s>, and give it to him.' He killed that calf, took the hide, and set out. That cow, out of love for her offspring, followed behind and behind, making lowing sounds. Having entered <s>Jetavana</s>, that cow stood at the gate of <s>Jetavana</s>, making lowing sounds. The Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are knowing and inquiring. The Buddha, the Blessed One, asks the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Why, <s>Ānanda</s>, does this cow stand at the gate of <s>Jetavana</s>?' The venerable <s>Ānanda</s> says: 'Blessed One, her calf was caused to be killed by the venerable <s>Upananda</s> for the purpose of leather. Therefore this cow stands at the gate of <s>Jetavana</s>, making lowing sounds.' The Blessed One said: 'Whatever disadvantage there is, monks, in monks keeping leather — therefore a monk should not keep leather. Those who keep it commit an offense.'

body.translated_text: Monks were wandering on a tour of the countryside. They came to a river. They were unable to cross while carrying their bowls and robes. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said: 'A monk should learn to swim.' The Group of Six crossed the <s>Ajiravatī</s> river, some going upstream, some downstream. Having crossed, they came [to women]: 'Sisters, we shall ferry you across — do it thus for yourselves.' By them the limbs and minor limbs of those [women] were touched. 'Come again!' They say: 'Those places which even our husbands have not touched, you have touched!' They reproach, criticize, and abuse [the monks]. The Blessed One said: 'Whatever disadvantage there is, monks, in touching women — therefore a monk should not touch a woman.'

The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said: 'She should be rescued.' Others say: 'Let go!' They are very strong. 'She should be released.' Others become motionless. Therefore a monk should not cross by holding a cow's tail. The Blessed One said: 'One should not cross by a cow's tail.' The monks had difficulty crossing rivers. They did not wish to cross by holding an elephant's tail. The Blessed One said: 'One may cross by holding the tail of five strong animals: a thoroughbred elephant, a thoroughbred horse, a bull, a buffalo, and a yak. Furthermore, one should cross by means of a raft.'

body.translated_text: The Group of Six cross by holding onto a cow's tail. A certain householder — his cows — they milked them more and more until the milk disappeared.

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'One should cross by means of a raft.' The Group of Six made [rafts] with colorful and variegated decorations, as large as lotuses, with images of men and women in amorous postures. They were seen by <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders, who said: 'Sirs, what is this?' They said: 'The Blessed One has permitted rafts.' They reproach: 'Noble ones, your asceticism is merely a sensual indulgence!' The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said: 'Monks should not keep rafts with colorful and variegated decorations, as large as lotuses, with images of men and women in amorous postures. Rather, two kinds of rafts are permitted: a saffron-colored one and a plain crossing raft.'

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'A monk should not keep wooden sandals.' Monks go into houses. Their sandals become soiled with mud. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said: 'Inside a house, a monk may keep wooden sandals.' Devout <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders offer wooden sandals to the monks of the <s>Saṃgha</s>. The monks do not accept them. They say: 'Noble ones, when the Blessed One had not yet arisen in the world, the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist ascetics) were the ones worthy of offerings.' Until the Blessed One said: 'They should be accepted. Having accepted them, they should be placed in the communal privy or the communal urinal.'

body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Wooden sandals shall not be worn.' They wore bamboo-leaf sandals. The same disadvantage arose. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Bamboo-leaf sandals shall not be worn.' They wore <s>muñja</s>-grass sandals. The same disadvantage arose. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Muñja</s>-grass sandals shall not be worn.' They wore rope sandals. The same disadvantage arose. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Rope sandals shall not be worn.' The monks reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Whoever has <s>vātaśoṇita</s> may wear rope sandals.'

children.translated_text: ) approached the dwelling of the venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> saw <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>'s walking path. Having seen it — and <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bhagavāns</s>, knowing, ask questions; they ask while already knowing — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, asked the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> about the walking path of the monk who exerts one-sidedly. 'It is <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>'s, Venerable One.' 'Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, I permit: <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s> shall wear single-layer sandals — not double-layered, not triple-layered. If those are subject to wear, a clasp may be added and they may be worn.' Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> approached the venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>. Having approached, he said to <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>: 'Know, venerable <s>Śroṇa</s>, that the Teacher has permitted you single-layer sandals, not double-layered' — and so on in detail. 'Is this, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, for the entire <s>Saṅgha</s> or for me alone?' 'For you alone.' 'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, the command of the Teacher is inviolable. If I were to wear them, my fellow monks would have cause to say: "Great indeed was what <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s> gained through going forth — he who, having abandoned <s>Campā</s> and an army of seven elephants, went forth, is now attached to a mere pair of sandals!" body.translated_text: When <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s> went forth, the group of six (<s>ṣaḍvargika</s>) saw gold-colored hairs four finger-breadths long on the soles of his feet. Having seen them, they said: 'This lump of butter — in a teaching of one-sided exertion, what will he accomplish by going forth?' He heard this. Having heard it, pride arose in him. He approached the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>. Having approached, he asked the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'What, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) of one-sided exertion spoken of by the <s>Bhagavān</s>?' body.translated_text: A certain elderly monk walked with shoes before the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to that monk: 'Move aside, monk! Do not stand before me.' Thereupon the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'That teacher who is besmeared with all worldly pleasures — even his disciples do not quickly and easily fall into sinful practices. How much more so when I dwell disjoined from all worldly pleasures!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> reflected: 'Whatever disadvantage there is, monks, in wearing shoes — therefore a monk shall not wear shoes.'

body.translated_text: A certain handsome one who had gone forth — his water-vessel was broken. Having washed his feet at the foot-washing place and filled his mouth with water, he set out walking with the gait of a peacock. The group of six (<s>ṣaḍvargika</s>) saw him. They said: 'Venerable ones, without music a monk is dancing! Play music!' They began playing mouth-music. They were rebuked by other monks: 'Why are you acting with levity?' They said: 'What levity is here? Do you not see a monk dancing without music?' The monks reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bhagavāns</s>, knowing, ask questions; they ask while already knowing. body.text: bhikṣor upānahāś chinnāḥ / sa carmakārasakāśaṃ gacchati / yāvad dīrghakālaṃ gatvā svabuddher vārayiṣyatīti / so 'nyatamena bhikṣuṇā dṛṣṭaḥ / yāvad asti mama kauśalaṃ yadi bhagavān anujānīyād granthayeyam* / etat prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti / bhagavān āha / yasya kauśalaṃ vidyate tena pratigupte pradeśe sthitvā granthayitavyam* / sa kathayati / bhagavatānujñātaḥ / granthaye / tatrārayā śastrakeṇa baddhikayā ca prayojanam* / etat prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti / bhagavān āha / tasmād anujānāmi bhikṣuṇā ārā śastrakaṃ baddhikā ca dhārayitavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: A monk's shoes were torn. He goes to a leather-worker. After going for a long time, he thought: 'He will put me off according to his own judgment.' He was seen by another monk, who said: 'I have the skill — if the <s>Bhagavān</s> would permit it, I would stitch them.' The monks reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'He who has the skill should stand in a secluded place and stitch them.' He said: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has permitted it. I shall stitch.' For that purpose, an awl, a blade, and a strap are needed. The monks reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore I permit — a monk should possess an awl, a blade, and a strap.'

body.translated_text: The <s>Carmavastu</s> (Chapter on Leather) is concluded.
